subject: dplyr: Extracting all distinct values and and and index of their position from columns of a (SQL) DB

messages.author: 01782de3c399f7d1
messages.subject: dplyr: Extracting all distinct values and and and index of their position from columns of a (SQL) DB
parts:
Hey,

My goal is to extract  
(1) all distinct values of x (<values>) and  
(2) which row in the data holds which distinct value (<index>), 
so that 
data.tmp$x == values[index]

In dplyr, I do something like the following in the moment:

> library(dplyr)
> 
> # create some test data ...
> set.seed(123141)
> data.tmp <- data.frame(x = round(rexp(1e2),1), id=1:1e2)
> data.tmp$x[1:10] <- NA                   
> # ... and copy to postgreSQL DB:
> db.postgres <- src_postgres("test", user='postgres', 
+                                      password='postgres',
+                                      host='localhost', port='5432')
> data <- copy_to(db.postgres, data.tmp)
> 
> 
> 
> # dense_rank() creates index of x-values, but destroys original row order:
> indextbl <- mutate(data, index=dense_rank(x))
> head(indextbl)
    x id index
1 0.0 94     1
2 0.0 56     1
3 0.0 92     1
4 0.0 32     1
5 0.0 95     1
6 0.1 44     2
> # use sql() to get distinct values: 
> ## how to chain this more efficiently to the first operation?
> distinctquery <- paste("SELECT * FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (x) x, index FROM (",  
+                         indextbl$query$sql, ") AS tmp1) AS tmp2 ORDER BY index")
> valuetbl <- tbl(indextbl$src, sql(distinctquery))
> head(valuetbl)
    x index
1 0.0     1
2 0.1     2
3 0.2     3
4 0.3     4
5 0.4     5
6 0.5     6
> 
> ## ... works, but means that the presumably expensive dense_rank() gets performed twice when
> ## collect()-ing in the lines below
> value <- collect(select(valuetbl, x))[,1]
> index <- collect(select(arrange(indextbl, id), index))[,1]
> all.equal(data.tmp$x, value[index])
[1] TRUE

My 2 questions:
1) is there a way to save intermediate tables in the database (i.e, indextbl above)?
2) is there a way to tell collect() that the return is all integers and not a data.frame with doubles to save memory/transfer time?

The motivation for this is that working with a (short) double vector that contains the <values>
and a long integer vector that holds the <index> allows for efficient representations of/computation with large model matrices: 
a design matrix for x can be represented as  
 X = S D  
 with a sparse, boolean n x d "sampling matrix" S that maps the n observations to the d distinct values (i.e, S_ij = I(x_i=values_j)) 
and a d x p design matrix for something like poly(<values>, df=<p>).  But first I have to get these two vectors from the data storage efficiently....

Any pointers anybody might have would be very much appreciated. 
Best,
Fabian

You can use compute() which works similarly to collect() except that
instead of returning a data frame to R, it creates a temporary table
in the database.

> 2) is there a way to tell collect() that the return is all integers and not
> a data.frame with doubles to save memory/transfer time?

No because it's probably not supported by the underlying driver
(RPostgreSQL), and I doubt that's the bottleneck anyway.
